description_en: In 1693 CE (NS 813), a group led by Guṇarāja Bhābo built a temple for Bhairava, the protector of Sānāgāũ, a village locally known as Thasi.Located east of the Gaṇeśa temple (SAN0020) in Sānāgāũ's Dyaḥnani, this south-facing temple has a three-tiered roof of traditional tiles crowned with three metallic finials, with the middle one adorned with a metallic parasol. An oblong metal banner (patāḥ) flag hangs from the middle finial down to the lower roof. Various utensils are nailed under the uppermost and middle roofs. Clad in embossed brass sheets, the entrance door is surmounted by a brasstoraṇadepicting the central figure of Bhairava flanked by Gaṇeśa and Kumāra.Inside the sanctum, Bhairava with six arms standing on a corpse is enshrined as the main deity. He is referred to as Mahākāla Bhairava in the inscriptions. The deities on the wooden toraṇa offered to Bhairava have been stolen. Inside the sanctum, facing west, is a statue of a devotee flanked by two women. The locals refer to the statue as Gāṃsyāḥ Āḥju while the women flanking him are probably his wives. There is no information about who Gāṃsyāḥ Āḥju was and his contributions to Sānāgāũ. Behind the temple, to the north, lies an aniconic stone stretching east-west. The stone is worshipped as Siddheśvara Mahādeva. This black stone was recovered when the forest was cleared for a new settlement in Sānāgāũ and was named Siddheśvara Mahādeva. According to a local saying, Sānāgāũ got its other name 'Siddhipura' from Siddheśvara Mahādeva (local resident, Maharjana, female, age 47).There are no historical records of the establishment of Bhairava in Sānāgāũ. It is likely that an open shrine was built for Bhairava as a protective deity at the beginning of the settlement in Sānāgāũ, but it is unclear when a temple was built for him. However, in 1626 CE (NS 746), a group led by Budha Baṃde and Kṛṣṇa Siṃha Bhāro laid traditional tiles on the roof. This record suggests that the open shrine was covered with a tiled roof. Later, in 1693 CE (NS 813), a group led by Guṇarāja Bhābo built a proper temple for Bhairava and offered a pair of flags as well. The name, Guṇarāja Bhābo, can be seen carved on a wooden component inside the sanctum.In 1699 CE (NS 819), during the reign of King Yoganarendra Malla, Suṣudeva Bhābo, Karirāma Bhābo, Jagadeva Bhābo, and others jointly offered a pair of stone lions to the temple. In 1849 CE (NS 969), Indralachami, along with her sons Dhanabṛdhi, Vīramuni, and Dharmmavīra, offered utensils and agricultural tools to the temple. In 1888 CE (NS 1008), Munirāja Bhāro, along with his wife Dhijalakṣmī, son Byakhā, and other family members, offered a brasstoraṇato the temple. After thistoraṇawas stolen, a new one was offered by Hareśa Maharjana and Tīrthamāyā Maharjana in 2021 CE(VS 2078).There is no designated priest for this temple. Locals worship Bhairava as part of their morning worship of the deities in the area. Every year, from the last day of Caitra to the 4th of Vaiśākha, a palanquin procession is carried out for Bhairava, along with Bālakumārī (SAN0030-002) in the Nāsaḥdyaḥ temple (SAN0030) and Gaṇeśa from the Gaṇeśa temple (SAN0020). On the first day, the metal statues of Bhairava, Bālakumārī, and Gaṇeśa kept inside the god-house (dyaḥchẽ) in Dyaḥnani are placed in separate palanquins in front of the temple for devotees to worship. On the 2nd of Vaiśākha, the three palanquins are taken around Sānāgāũ for a procession. On the 3rd of Vaiśākha, a government worship is performed with thedvāres of Sānāgāũ carrying of the worship representing the government. On the evening of the 4th of Vaiśākha, the deities are reinstated to their usual seats inside thedyaḥchẽ.Every year on Śrīpañcamī, the 5th of the bright fortnight of Māgha, special worship of Gāṃsyāḥ Āḥju is performed by a religious trust formed for this specific purpose. On the 10th of the bright fortnight of Āśvina, a sword procession (pāyāḥ) is taken out in Sānāgāũ. The person carrying the sword on the occasion first offers homage to Bhairava before chopping an ash gourd as a symbol of the elimination of evil entities.
description_ne: सानागाउँका रक्षकको रूपमा स्थापना गरिएका भैरवको लागि नेसं ८१३ (सन् १६९३) मा गुणराज भावो प्रमुख रहेको समूहले मन्दिर निर्माण गरिदिएको थियो । प्रत्येक वर्ष चैत्र मसान्तदेखि वैशाख ४ गतेसम्म भैरवका साथमा द्य: ननिमा रहेका गणेश र बालकुमारीको खटजात्रा गरिन्छ ।सानागाउँको द्य: ननिमा रहेको गणेश मन्दिर (SAN0020) को पूर्वमा भैरव मन्दिर अवस्थित रहेको छ । दक्षिणाभिमुख गरी निर्माण गरिएको यस मन्दिरमा तीन तह झिङ्गटीका छाना राखिएका छन् । मन्दिरमा तीनवटा धातुका गजूर राखिएका छन् । ती गजूरमध्ये बीचको गजूरमा धातुको छत्र ओढाइएको छ । बीचको गजूरदेखि तल्लो छानासम्म पुग्ने गरी धातुको पता: झुण्ड्याइएको छ । सबभन्दा माथिल्लो र बीचको छानामुनि कीला ठोकेर भाँडाकुँडाहरू चढाइएका छन् । मन्दिरको गर्भगृहभित्र प्रवेश गर्ने ढोकामा पित्तलको पाताले मोडिएको छ । ढोकामाथि पित्तलको पाताले मोडिएको तोरण राखिएको छ । तोरणको मध्यभागमा भैरव र दायाँ-बायाँ गणेश र कुमार राखिएका छन् । गर्भगृहभित्र शवमाथि उभिएका छ हात भएका भैरवलाई मुख्य देवताको रूपमा स्थापना गरिएको छ । स्थानीयहरूले भैल:द्य: भनी पूजा गर्ने यस देवतालाई अभिलेखमा महाकाल भैरव भनिएको छ । भैरवलाई चढाइएको काष्ठतोरणमा रहेका देवताहरू चोरी भइसकेका छन् । गर्भगृहभित्र पश्चिमाभिमुख गरी एकजना भक्तको मूर्ति स्थापना गरिएको छ । उनको दायाँबायाँ दुईजना महिलाहरू पनि रहेका छन् । स्थानीयहरू उनलाई गांस्या: आ:जुको नामले सम्बोधन गर्छन् । दायाँबायाँ रहेका दुई महिलाहरू उनका श्रीमतीहरू हुनसक्छन् । गांस्याः आःजु को थिए र उनले सानागाउँमा कुन कीर्ति स्थापना गरेका थिए भन्नेबारे कुनै जानकारी पाइँदैन । मन्दिरको पछाडि उत्तरपट्टि पूर्व-पश्चिम फैलिएको आकृतिविहीन ढुङ्गा रहेको छ । उक्त ढुङ्गालाई सिद्धेश्वर महादेव मानी पूजा गरिन्छ । थसिमा बस्ती बसाउन जङ्गल फँडानी गर्दा उक्त कालो ढुङ्गा फेला परेको थियो । जङ्गलभित्र सिद्ध भएर बसेको हुनाले त्यस ढुङ्गालाई सिद्धेश्वर महादेव भनेर नामकरण गरिएको थियो । उनै सिद्धेश्वर महादेवको नामबाट सानागाउँको अर्को नाम 'सिद्धिपुर' रहन गएको भन्ने लोकभनाइ रहेको छ (Local resident from a Maharjan caste, female, age 47) ।सानागाउँका रक्षकको रूपमा पुजिने यी भैरवको स्थापना बारे कुनै अभिलेख पाइँदैन । सानागाउँमा बस्ती बस्न थालेदेखि नै रक्षक देवताको रूपमा देवस्थल बनाएर यी भैरवको स्थापना गरिएको हुनसक्छ । पहिले खुल्ला ठाउँमा राखिएको भैरवको देवस्थलमा नेसं ७४६ (सन् १६२६) मा झिङ्गटीको छाना छाउने काम गरिएको थियो । उक्त काम गर्ने समूहमा बुध बंदे र कृष्णसिङ भारो प्रमुख थिए भने जिवराज भावो, जिकिसिंङ, रूपराम, बुधचन्द आदि व्यक्तिहरू सहयोगीको रूपमा रहेका थिए । नेसं ८१३ (सन् १६९३) मा गुणराज भावो प्रमुख रहेको समूहले देवस्थलको रूपमा मात्र रहेको भैरवको लागि मन्दिर निर्माण गरी दायाँबायाँ झण्डा पनि चढाएको थियो । गुणराज भावोको नाम गर्भगृहभित्र काठमा कुँदिएको देख्न सकिन्छ । नेसं ८१९ (सन् १६९९) मा राजा योगनरेन्द्र मल्लको राज्यकालमा सुषुदेव भावो, करिराम भावो, जगदेव भावो लगायतका व्यक्तिहरूले मिलेर एक जोडी सिंह सिंह चढाएका थिए । नेसं ९६९ (सन् १८४९) मा इन्द्रलछमी (इन्द्रलक्ष्मी) ले छोराहरू धनवृधि, वीरमुनि, धर्म्मवीरसँग मिलेर मन्दिरमा भाँडाकुँडाहरू, खेतमा काम गर्ने ज्यावलहरू चढाएकी थिइन् । नेसं १००८ (सन् १८८८) मा मुनिराज भारोले श्रीमती धिजलक्ष्मी, छोरा ब्यखा लगायत परिवारका सदस्यहरूसँग मिलेर मन्दिरमा पित्तलको तोरण चढाएका थिए । उक्त तोरण चोरी भएपछि विसं २०७८ (सन् २०२१) मा हरेश महर्जन र तीर्थमाया महर्जनले मिलेर नयाँ तोरण चढाएका थिए ।यस मन्दिरमा पूजारी भनी कुनै व्यक्ति नियुक्त गरिएको छैन । स्थानीयहरूले बिहान देवीदेवताहरूको पूजा गर्ने सिलसिलामा यस मन्दिरमा पनि पूजा गर्छन् । प्रत्येक वर्ष चैत्र महिनाको मसान्तदेखि वैशाख ४ गतेसम्म भैरवका साथमा द्यः ननिमा रहेको नासःद्यः मन्दिर(SAN0030)भित्र अवस्थित बालकुमारी (SAN0030-002) र गणेश मन्दिर (SAN0020) भित्र रहेको गणेशको खटजात्रा गरिन्छ । जात्राको पहिलो दिन चैत्र मसान्तमा द्यः ननिमा रहेको द्यःछेँभित्र राखिएका बालकुमारी, भैरव र गणेशको धातुको मूर्तिलाई द्यःछेँ बाहिर ल्याइन्छ । ती मूर्तिहरूलाई अलग-अलग खटमा राखेर आ-आफ्नो मन्दिर बाहिर राखिन्छ । त्यहाँ भक्तजनहरूले पूजा गर्छन् । वैशाख १ गतेसम्म तीनवटै खटलाई मन्दिर बाहिर राखेर पूजा गराइन्छ । वैशाख २ गते ती देवताहरूको खटजात्रा गरी सानागाउँ परिक्रमा गराइन्छ । वैशाख ३ गते सरकारी पूजा गरिन्छ । सानागाउँका द्वारेहरूले सरकारको प्रतिनिधित्व गरी पूजा गर्छन् । वैशाख ४ गते साँझ देवताहरूलाई खटबाट निकालेर द्यःछेँभित्र लगेर पहिलेकै स्थानमा पुनर्स्थापना गरिन्छ । प्रत्येक वर्ष माघ शुक्ल ५ (श्रीपञ्चमी) को दिनमा गांस्याः आःजुको पूजा गरिन्छ । त्यसको लागि छुट्टै गुठी नै गठन गरिएको छ । प्रत्येक वर्ष दशैंको टीका (आश्विन शुक्ल १०) मा सानागाउँमा खड्गजात्रा निकालिन्छ । त्यस दिन खड्ग बोक्ने व्यक्तिले भैरवको दर्शन गरी पूजा गरिसकेपछि मात्र कुभिण्डो काट्नुपर्ने परम्परा रहेको छ ।

historical_events.event_name: Roofing of the Bhairava shrine with tiles
historical_events.event_description: A group led by Budha Baṃde and Kṛṣṇa Siṃha Bhāro laid traditional tiles on the roof of the Bhairava shrine. Other individuals like Jivarāja Bhābo, Jikisiṃṅa, Rūparāma, Budhacanda, and others also assisted the work. One-fourth of the tiles required for the roof was sponsored by a person named Rūpa, while the rest were contributed by other members of the group. This record suggests that the open shrine was covered with a tiled roof.
A group led by Guṇarāja Bhābo built a proper temple for Bhairava and offered a pair of flags as well. Individuals like Jogideva, Mahāmuṇi, and Suṣurideva were also involved in the group.

During the reign of King Yoganarendra Malla, Suṣudeva Bhābo, Karirāma Bhābo, Jagadeva Bhābo, and others jointly offered a pair of stone lions to the temple. Two local administrators, Karyāsiṃha and Jayakṛṣṇa, were appointed aspramāṇaof Sānāgāũ at the time of this event.

historical_events.event_name: Offering metal utensils and farming tools
historical_events.event_description: Indralachami, along with her sons Dhanabṛdhi, Vīramuni, and Dharmmavīra, offered utensils and agricultural tools to the temple.
Together with his wife Dhijalakṣmī, son Byakhā, and other family members, Munirāja Bhāro offered a brasstoraṇato the temple.
Kuṃbha Bhāro and his family from Sānāgāũ offered two brasstoraṇas to Bhairava.
A community group with Muni Thākuli as the most senior member installed a bell at the temple.
Kavi Prasāda erected a stone pillar in Sānāgāũ after organizing devotional singing dedicated to Viṣṇu and hosting a feast for brahmins.
Tulsībahādura Maharjana offered an oblong banner (patāḥ) to the temple.

historical_events.event_name: Offering of trident to Siddheśvara Mahādeva
historical_events.event_description: Kṛṣṇagopāla Maharjana, Nāti Maharjana, Ajaya Maharjana, Lakṣmī Maharjana, and family members offered a trident to Siddheśvara Mahādeva.
After the oldtoraṇawas stolen from the temple, a new one was installed by Hareśa Maharjana and Tīrthamāyā Maharjana.

historical_events.event_name: Offering of a garland of bells
historical_events.event_description: A group led by Siṃghavīra offered a garland of small bells to the temple.
Byakhāsiṃ, Rāmanārāṃ, Harṣamāna, and others installed a bell at the temple. After the bell was stolen, a new bell (SAN0010-006) was installed in 1889 CE (NS 1009).
